title: Endpoint SLI fingerprinting, error-budget escrow, and staged circuit-breaker choreography for conversational bursts
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem: Bursty conversational routes (session-based chat) show highly variable tail latency and quality regressions when KV cache eviction or model-variant failover occurs. Current SLI aggregation groups these routes with generic endpoint metrics which hides per-session degradations and leads to late detection and broad throttles that unnecessarily impact healthy tenants.

Goal: Define a reproducible per-endpoint SLI fingerprint and establish an error-budget escrow mechanism that can be deducted / credited during staged circuit-breaker activations. The fingerprinting should incorporate request shape (token distribution), KV cache hit-rate impact, and recent model-variant quality deltas. The escrow enables safe short-term crediting for routes with known cache-sensitive characteristics while preserving global error-budget governance.

Outcomes expected: clear SLI definitions per endpoint variant, a math for escrow accounting and reconciliation, and a choreography for staged circuit-breaker triggers that progressively shed load from affected variants to fallback variants or regional capacity while minimizing user-visible quality regressions.
proposed_solution:
1) Define an SLI fingerprint model: for each route, publish a compact fingerprint consisting of median/95/99 latency, avg prompt token count, KV cache hit-rate, and last-24h quality delta (eval metric).
2) Implement an error-budget escrow ledger: each endpoint has a short-lived escrow bucket (minutes to hours) that can be borrowed against for transient cache churn events; borrows are logged with reason tags (cache-eviction, model-rollout, region-eject).
3) Staged circuit-breaker choreography: three stages - warn (route-level throttles/latency SLO relaxation signals to caller), soft-shed (reduce concurrency/burst window, route-specific queue timeouts), hard-shed (fall back to pinned cheaper variant or regional redirect). Each stage consumes from escrow differently and emits structured events for the Console.
4) Telemetry and reconciliation: instrument new fingerprint metrics and escrow transactions; reconcile escrow weekly with global error-budget transfers and produce alerts when escrow utilization crosses thresholds.
5) Rollout: start with 10 high-traffic conversational routes in us-west, observe for 2 weeks, iterate rules, then expand to multiregion pilot.
acceptance_criteria: SLI fingerprint schema documented and stored in Console metadata for endpoints
Escrow ledger implemented and exposes borrow/repay events in tracing and cost dashboards
Circuit-breaker stages implemented with configurable thresholds per fingerprint
End-to-end test demonstrates a burst that would previously trigger global shedding now contained to affected route with <10% additional global error-budget burn
Runbook and Playbook updated with example incident workflow and rollback steps
